questions.title: Which player will command the highest transfer fee paid by a Premier League club during the 2026 summer transfer window?
questions.background: This question concerns completed transfers into Premier League clubs ahead of the 2026–27 season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve using Al Jazeera Sport's reporting of completed transfers after England's 2026 summer transfer window closes. The answer is the player whose transfer fee, expressed in pounds sterling, is the highest paid by a Premier League club during that window. Exclude proposed or failed transfers. Accepted Answer Format : The player's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Significant 2026-08-30 updates narrow the two-horse race between Bradley Barcola and Enzo Fernandez ahead of Tuesday's Sept 1 deadline. On Barcola's side, Source of Truth Al Jazeera Sport (Aug 30, Van Dijk/Gakpo article) explicitly cites Barcola's Liverpool package as rising to $166m (£123m = £106m initial + £17m add-ons per Aug 29 Al Jazeera/BBC) and calls him 'the second-most expensive player in Premier League history,' confirming Al Jazeera ranks total package values above Morgan Rogers (£117m) and Elliot Anderson (£116m). However, on Enzo Fernandez's side: (1) market.csv (qid 876325) already confirms Enzo completes a permanent transfer to Manchester City this window; (2) Al Jazeera (Aug 30 Chelsea-Brighton report) notes Enzo missed a second straight match with his future still unresolved before Tuesday's deadline; and (3) FootballTransfers (Aug 30, citing The Telegraph's Matt Law) reports City missed Chelsea's earlier €140m (£120m) unofficial deadline and Chelsea have now RAISED their asking price above £120m as time runs out. Because £120m was only £3m shy of Barcola's £123m, a late Chelsea price hike (or any base-fee comparison against Barcola's £106m initial) gives Enzo a much stronger shot to top Barcola than yesterday's 37% implied. Shifting Bradley Barcola 0.58 -> 0.52 and Enzo Fernandez 0.37 -> 0.44, trimming Morgan Rogers 0.03 -> 0.02, nudging Julian Alvarez 0.005 -> 0.012 (Al Jazeera Aug 30 notes Arsenal as the only viable alternative at €150m after Arsenal raised funds selling Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus), and Elliot Anderson 0.003 -> 0.002 (sum = 0.994).

questions.background: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) publishes a monthly index tracking international prices across major food commodity categories.
questions.resolution_criteria: Resolve to the commodity category with the largest percentage price increase from July to August 2026, as reported in the FAO's September 2026 Food Price Index release. Resolution Date: 2026-09-04 Answer with the category name.

questions.title: Which Southeast Asian country will declare a state of emergency over wildfire haze between September 1 and September 5, 2026?
questions.background: Seasonal wildfire smoke can cross borders in Southeast Asia, creating public-health risks and prompting emergency government responses.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official national government announcements, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the country whose national authorities announce a formal state of emergency because of wildfire haze between September 1 and September 5, 2026, inclusive. The declaration may cover the entire country or a specific area within it. Air-quality warnings, school closures, or health advisories without a formal emergency declaration do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country’s common English name.
